scopes.title: From anywhere in Windows
scopes.learn: These keys work in any program, with no axKit window open: they bring an axKit app up. Each is a setting of its app and can be changed there.

scopes.title: The same in every axKit window
scopes.learn: These keys do the same kind of thing in every window of axKit, so they are learned once.

scopes.title: Inside one app's window
scopes.learn: These keys belong to the window you are in. The pattern says what kind of thing the key does; what exactly it does depends on the app.

note: The families of SPEC AX-8.18's rules. The first keys moved for them on 2026-11-16: the places and views of axClaude, axTerminal, axGIT and axProcess went to Alt+1, 2 and 3 (SPEC AX-8.14), and Ctrl+Slash and Ctrl+Period were added (AX-8.15). The maintainer settled every family on 2026-11-26 and the keys moved the same day (AX-8.18): a moved key is no misfit, and each misfit left is an exception kept on purpose, its reason in its kind. No test holds a key to its family. Each family is a pattern of keys and the one kind of thing such a key would do. A misfit is a command of docs/axKit/window-commands.json on a key of the pattern that does another kind of thing; 'does' is the command's label there, 'kind' is what kind of thing it is instead. 'windows' names the keys of a pattern that are Windows' own (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+S and the like), which stay as every Windows user knows them and are not counted as misfits. tools/key-map.ps1 checks that every key named here is of its family's pattern and that every command named here is in the inventory, and writes the families at the end of docs/axKit/key-map.md. 'learn' is the family as a user is told it, one or two sentences for the ear; the script writes docs/axKit/key-groups.md from it, the keys by group, which is the page a user learns the keys from. A family with 'source': 'system-wide' takes its keys from BundleKeys.SystemWide (the hotkeys, which are in no window's inventory).

families.does: bring up axKit from anywhere in Windows
families.learn: Hold Ctrl and Shift and press Space or a punctuation key, in any program: an axKit app comes up. These are the only keys of axKit that work outside its windows (SPEC AX-8.11).

families.does: the in-window partner of the same key with Ctrl+Shift
families.learn: Ctrl and a punctuation key stays inside the window you are in, where the same key with Ctrl and Shift works from anywhere. Ctrl+Slash asks Claude about this window, as Shift+F1 does; with Shift added it brings up axHelp's conversation from any program. Ctrl+Period opens the Context menu, as Shift+F10 does; its partner with Shift is kept for later. Ctrl+Comma opens the command palette, as F1 does, a second key on trial; with Shift added it brings up axClip's search from anywhere.

families.does: select, or toggle
families.learn: Space selects the thing you are on in a list of things you can act on several of at once, and deselects it again (the maintainer's rule of 2026-11-22, SPEC AX-8.16: axFile, axTask and axMedia so far). On a check box it checks and unchecks. Ctrl+Space switches between navigating and editing.

families.does: act on what is selected
families.learn: Ctrl and a letter does something to what you are on, and the letter is the first letter of the command where it can be: Ctrl+I interrupts, Ctrl+K bookmarks the line, Ctrl+R runs or fetches. The keys every Windows program has (copy, paste, save, find) are the same here, and Ctrl+N makes a new one of what the window holds: a document in the editors, a session in axClaude and axTerminal, a window in axFile, axMedia and axPreview. In a text, Ctrl with NVDA's browse-mode letter jumps while you type: Ctrl+H the next heading, Ctrl+K a link.

families.does: the window's own numbered action
families.learn: Ctrl and a number is the window's own numbered action (SPEC AX-8.18 rule 3). In a text or a list with headings, Ctrl and a number from 1 to 6 goes to the next heading of that level; in axTask, Ctrl and a number from 1 to 9 runs that action key of the list.

families.does: go to the previous heading of that level
families.learn: Adding Shift to Ctrl and a number goes backwards: the previous heading of that level.

families.does: go to a place or view of the window
families.learn: Alt and a number goes to one of the window's main places or views: the first, the second, the third, in axClaude, axTerminal, axGIT and axProcess; Alt+0 is All tasks in axTask. A place is never on Ctrl and a number.

families.does: the reverse or the wider form of the same letter with Ctrl
families.learn: Adding Shift to Ctrl and a letter gives the reverse or the bigger form of that command. A letter or a number is always inside the window; Space or punctuation with Ctrl+Shift is always the whole of axKit.

acts on the program; as in a web browser, Ctrl+Shift+R is the heavier reload, the same key as axTerminal's

families.does: open a standalone app
families.learn: Ctrl with a function key opens a standalone axKit app from any axKit window, in the order of the Window menu (SPEC AX-8.18 rule 6). Which key opens which app is written on the page of the apps, apps.md, and in each window's F1 text.

families.does: open an access layer
families.learn: Ctrl+Shift with a function key opens an access layer, an app over a program you install, from any axKit window, in the order of the Window menu (SPEC AX-8.18 rule 6).

families.does: say or show
families.learn: A function key alone says or shows, the same in every window: F7 reads in full what you are on, F8 reads it with details, F9 says the status, F11 shows the text another way, F12 opens the field to go to a line, a folder or a time. F1 opens the command palette, palette and help in one: with nothing typed, the rules of the keys and the window's keys. F2 rename, F3 find next, F4 send a report, F5 refresh and F6 the other pane are Windows' own keys, kept as Windows taught them.

families.does: the reverse or the other form of the same F-key
families.learn: Shift with a function key is that key's other form: Shift+F3 finds the previous, Shift+F1 asks Claude about the window instead of reading the help. Shift+F10 is Windows' own key for the context menu, and the Applications key does the same.

families.does: open or confirm
families.learn: Enter opens what you are on or says yes to a question.

families.pattern: Enter with Ctrl, Shift or Alt
families.does: another form of open or confirm
families.learn: Enter with a modifier is another way of opening or saying yes. Ctrl+Enter does the most frequent action where you are: it sends the message or the command, commits, saves a form, marks a task done in axTask, or pauses and resumes in axMedia. Shift+Enter opens what you are on another way, such as a preview. Alt+Enter shows its properties and Ctrl+Shift+Enter starts a program as administrator, as everywhere in Windows; in axClaude it sends the queued messages now, another form of Ctrl+Enter.

families.does: go back or close; with Shift, Escape sent to the program under the window
families.learn: Escape only goes back one step or closes what is open; it never clears what you typed and never loses work without asking. Shift+Escape sends Escape to the terminal's program in axTerminal.

families.does: remove
families.learn: Delete removes what you are on, and what can be lost asks first or can be undone. Ctrl+Delete clears what you typed: a list's filter, axCalc's field. Ctrl+Shift+Delete clears a whole history, as in a web browser: axCalc's and axClip's history, axTerminal's transcript.

families.does: move between panes
families.learn: Ctrl+Tab goes to the next part of the window and Ctrl+Shift+Tab to the one before.

families.pattern: The arrows, Page Up, Page Down, Tab, Shift+Tab and Backspace
families.does: move through what you are on
families.learn: The arrows and Page Up and Page Down move through a list or a text, as in every Windows program. In a list of levels, Right arrow goes in and Left arrow or Backspace comes back out; on a field with a choice of values, Left and Right arrow choose the value. Tab and Shift+Tab go to the next and the previous part of the window.

families.pattern: Shift with an arrow, Home, End or Space
families.does: select
families.learn: Shift with an arrow, Home or End selects as it moves, as in every Windows list and text. Shift+Space selects from the nearest selected thing to here. The keys, their words and their code are one shared piece (SPEC AX-8.16).

families.pattern: Ctrl with an arrow, Home or End, and Ctrl+Shift with Left or Right arrow
families.does: a bigger step
families.learn: Ctrl with an arrow takes a bigger step: Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down go to the previous and the next section, Ctrl+Left and Ctrl+Right go back and forward 15 seconds in a recording. Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End go to the first and the last. With Shift too, a bigger step still: the previous or the next file.

families.does: the choices of what you are on
families.learn: Alt with an arrow is for the choices of what you are on, in the arrows' own directions (the maintainer's rule of 2026-11-21): Alt+Right goes into the list of them, where the arrows move and Enter chooses; Alt+Down and Alt+Up change to the next and the previous one in place; Alt+Left steps out to what is around it and offers what can be added there. axMedia's speed is Alt+Up and Alt+Down, axTerminal's recent commands Alt+Down in the command field. Ctrl with an arrow moves the cursor a bigger step, and moving an item of a list up or down is Ctrl+Shift+Up and Ctrl+Shift+Down, wherever a list has it.

families.does: make the text larger or smaller
families.learn: Ctrl+Plus makes the text larger and Ctrl+Minus smaller, in every window, as in a web browser.

families.does: in a view you read, a quick command: go to the next thing of a kind, or say something
families.learn: Where you read and do not type (a text in navigation mode, a preview), a letter alone is a command: H goes to the next heading and Shift+H to the one before, L says the line. In a text's navigation mode, a letter that moves plays a high tick first, and a letter with no command plays a wooden bonk.

families.does: open a menu
families.learn: Alt and a letter opens the menu that starts with that letter, as in every Windows program.
